newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hits out at Israel over settlements.
newsitem.headline: France hits out at Israel over settlements.

text.p: France on Wednesday said Israel was breaching its peace accord with the PLO by encouraging settlements in Palestinian autonomous territories.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a news briefing that Israel's settlement policy was contrary to the 1995 accord on autonomy which bars changes in Gaza and the West Bank pending negotiations on their final status.

"French authorities are convinced that peace and security in the Middle East are possible only if agreed deals are being respected. They hope that the Israeli governmemt abides by its commitment," Rummelhardt said.
He was commenting on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's first visit to a Jewish settlement on the West Bank on Tuesday, which also drew a sharp rebuke from Washington.
He said Netanyahu's comments during his visit to the settlement of Ariel had been "extremely worrying". The hardline Israeli premier asked: "Why not develop communities here?"

Netanyahu's visit to the West Bank, just one day after the Palestinian Authority called for an immediate halt to all settlement activity, was a show of defiance to Palestinians opposed to his policy of expanding the outposts.
